past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: To push the liquid up in a straw, the air pressure inside the straw will
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: When sucking on a straw, air is removed from inside the straw, causing the air pressure inside the straw to decrease. The higher atmospheric pressure on the liquid's surface outside then pushes the liquid up into the straw.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: A parcel box of weight 500 N is placed on a table. If the area of the bottom of the box is measured as 0.50 m2, then the pressure exerted by the box on the table will be

In a magic show, a performer lies down on a bed of nails without any injury. However, when the same performer steps on a single nail, it goes right through his foot. With reference to the given situation, which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: A. The area is same in both the cases, but more force is applied on the bed of nails.
B. The force remains the same, but more pressure is applied on the bed of nails.
C. More force is exerted on a single nail than on the entire bed of nails.
D. Force increases, but less pressure is applied on the bed of nails.
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: When lying on a bed of nails, the weight (force) of the performer is distributed over a large number of contact points (large area), resulting in small pressure per nail. When stepping on a single nail, the entire weight acts on a single tiny area, creating extremely high pressure.

crqs.question: Write any THREE differences between evaporation and boiling.
crqs.answer: 1. Evaporation occurs at any temperature, whereas boiling occurs only at the fixed boiling point. 2. Evaporation takes place only at the liquid surface, whereas boiling occurs throughout the liquid volume with bubble formation. 3. Evaporation causes cooling, whereas temperature remains constant during boiling.
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I 2025 Annual Paper II Q.4

crqs.question: The temperature of a metal rim is increased before fixing it onto a wooden cartwheel. Give a scientific reason.
crqs.answer: Heating causes thermal expansion of the metal rim, increasing its diameter so it slips easily over the wooden wheel; upon cooling, it contracts tightly onto the wheel.
crqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I Model Paper II Q.4

erqs.question: Explain the temperature–time heating curve when crushed ice at -10°C is slowly heated until it turns into steam at 100°C, identifying why the temperature remains constant during melting and boiling.
erqs.answer: During melting at 0°C (latent heat of fusion) and boiling at 100°C (latent heat of vaporisation), absorbed heat energy goes into overcoming intermolecular forces rather than increasing average translational kinetic energy, so temperature stays constant.
erqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-I Sample Practical Paper III
